claim.statement: A finite set $\mathcal H\subset\mathbb N$ is \emph{admissible} if for every prime $q$ there is a residue class modulo $q$ containing no element of $\mathcal H$.

For a predicate $P$ on $\mathbb N$ and $k\ge j\ge1$, let $\DHL_P[k,j]$ be the statement: for every admissible $\mathcal H$ with $|\mathcal H|=k$ there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\#\{h\in\mathcal H: P(n+h)\}\ge j$. Write $\DHL[k,j]$ for $\DHL_P[k,j]$ with $P$ = primality.
For $c\in\mathbb N$ write $H_1\le c$ for the statement that $p_{n+1}-p_n\le c$ for infinitely many $n$. For an integer-valued sequence this is equivalent to $\liminf_{n}(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le c$.

claim.statement: A given sieve method establishes $\DHL[k,j]$ only if $j\le\lceil k/2\rceil$.
claim.title: Parity barrier

claim.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item Under \cref{hyp:parity}, a sieve method establishing $\DHL[k,2]$ has $k\ge3$. \item (Unconditional.) No admissible $3$-element set is contained in an interval $[a,a+5]$. Together with \cref{lem:adm}, the minimal diameter of an admissible $3$-set is exactly $6$. \end{enumerate}
